summary: A 1970 note announcing or discussing a network meeting by Steve Crocker. It is administrative.
subtitle: Notice of a network research group meeting in November 1970.

tldr.problem: The network research community needed to meet and discuss practical issues.
tldr.mechanism: Steve Crocker scheduled a meeting during the Fall Joint Computer Conference in Houston, announcing it via RFC with a proposed agenda of four topics and an invitation for additional discussion items.
tldr.outcome: The meeting took place as planned and resulted in RFC 77, which documented the discussions and decisions made.

today: RFC 75 is an Internet Experiment document. It is historically significant as part of the early administrative communication that coordinated the growing network community.

sections.title: Meeting Announcement
sections.content: RFC 75 is an administrative notice by Steve Crocker announcing a meeting of the Network Working Group. The meeting was scheduled for 8 p.m. on Monday, November 16, 1970, in room Astro VII of the Astroworld Hotel in Houston, Texas, taking advantage of the Fall Joint Computer Conference (FJCC) being held there.
sections.eli5: An announcement of when and where a big meeting would happen.

sections.title: Proposed Topics
sections.content:
The RFC listed four main topics for discussion: accounting mechanisms for resource usage, documentation distribution to sites, person-to-person message sending and message storage, and access policies for foreign users. The notice also invited attendees to propose additional topics for discussion.

To help with logistics, Crocker asked prospective attendees to notify his secretary, Benita Kirstel, to ensure the room was large enough, though unexpected attendees were also welcome.
sections.eli5: The author suggested a few things to discuss: how to keep track of who uses what, how to share documentation, how to send messages between people, and who should be allowed to use remote computers.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: This brief RFC served its administrative purpose and the meeting did occur. The discussions at the FJCC meetings were later documented in RFC 77 (Network Meeting Report), which recorded decisions on protocol improvements, TELNET specification, accounting schemes, and the role of the Network Information Center.
sections.eli5: The meeting happened, people discussed the topics, and what they decided on got written down in another document.
